notes:
Snapshot: mid-market product analytics SaaS; primary goal embed assistant into the product and migrate heavy embedding workloads to Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and cost. Evaluated hosted API in January (trial), ran sandbox POC in Feb. Preference: start on Hosted for integration speed, then move to Dedicated (reserved capacity + VPC) once Q3 usage growth kicks in.

Recent activity / timeline:
- 2026-01-18: Intro demo (AE Jordan + SE Priya). Quick walkthrough of hosted API, streaming, embeddings.
- 2026-02-04: Hosted trial onboarded, ingested product docs for semantic search; latency ~120ms p50 for small queries; 95th pctl around 420ms on hosted trial during spike.
- 2026-02-12: Technical deep-dive (Fireflies ff_2026-02-12_9f4b123). SE discussed batching and KV caching; customer asked about persistent KV across Dedicated nodes.
- 2026-03-02: Legal + procurement call (Fireflies ff_2026-03-02_ae2938). Customer submitted MSA/DPA redlines (see Drive). Requested stronger SLA credit and explicit data residency in EU region for some customers.
- 2026-03-05: Pricing follow-up from AE — customer prefers committed monthly billing vs. per-token for predictability; asked for blended rate for embeddings + generation.
- POC plan: small Dedicated pool (2 GPUs) demo for 4 weeks to validate throughput 50 req/s and 95p <200ms for short chat flows. POC infra scoped; SE to provide deployment manifest and expected cost delta.

Key requirements and asks (from product + infra):
- Latency: target 95th percentile < 200ms for single-turn chat under steady-state (50 req/s).
- Throughput: sustained 50-100 requests/sec for embeddings pipeline batch windows.
- Model support: prefer open-model variants compatible with Llama-2 family and quantized ops. Want roadmap for multi-arch kernel support.
- Routing/fallback: need automatic fallback to a lower-cost model during Dedicated maintenance windows.
- Security: SSO (SAML), SOC2 attestation, audit logging export, KMS integration for key management, DPA with EU data residency clause.

Procurement / legal notes (what they redlined):
- MSA: stronger indemnity carveouts; narrower termination for convenience window; clarified IP ownership for prompts/outputs.
- SLA: requested 99.95% availability and service credits tiered at 4 hours downtime. SE recommended standard 99.9% plus business continuity playbook.
- DPA: requested 30-day maximum retention for transient logs and explicit EU residency for EU customers. Also wants a signed subprocessors list.
- Onboarding: vendor onboarding questionnaire (security questionnaire) completed — pending SOC2 report upload and ISO gap answers.

Pricing / commercial:
- Looking at committed monthly Dedicated plan vs. hosted at scale. Procurement prefers a committed monthly price band to fit forecasting. Target ARR band shared: $75k-$250k.
- Wants clarity on overage handling, burst capacity pricing, and reserved GPU pool SLAs.

Quotes / direct lines from calls:
- "We can live on hosted for a short runway, but predictability is everything — we need reserved capacity before our next funding milestone." — Dir. of Product.
- "If SLA and DPA are acceptable, legal said they can sign within 2 weeks." — Procurement lead.

Next steps (action items owner):
- AE (Jordan): deliver final commercial term sheet with blended rate options (by 2026-03-15).
- SE (Priya): provide Dedicated deployment manifest + expected perf numbers (by 2026-03-12).
- Legal (Sunvale): send consolidated redlines; Redwood legal to respond with tracked changes (target initial response 3 business days).
- Infra/Onboarding: schedule Dedicated POC start date (tentative 2026-04-01) pending MSA/DPA agreement.

Notes/observations: customer is price-sensitive but values predictable latency and enterprise controls. Procurement is pragmatic — main blockers are MSA/DPA language and SLA credits. Risk: if legal negotiation drags >4 weeks, customer may pilot alternative vendor or postpone Dedicated until next quarter.
